script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 13. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Your heart beats, your lungs breathe, you walk in steps—your body runs on rhythm.  Music organizes sound into beats.  Seasons cycle through years.

Your body is a collection of rhythms: heartbeat, breathing, brain waves, sleep cycles. These aren't random—they're oscillating systems that keep you alive. External rhythms can entrain internal ones, which is why music affects your pulse. When people move to the same rhythm, something happens: they feel connected.  Marching, dancing, singing together—shared rhythm creates social bonds.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Life has rhythm.  Finding your patterns—daily routines, work flows, energy cycles—creates flow and reduces resistance.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Rhythm Awareness - Find Your Beats.

Here's your activity: Map your energy rhythms today—when are you most alert? Most creative? Most tired? Notice if you're working with or against your natural rhythms. Like finding a beat in music, finding your daily rhythm creates flow. This helps you notice personal and environmental rhythms.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the beat in everything can be applied to rhythm awareness - find your beats. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
